en: Hahaha, you're a funny guy, Saejima! Hey, maybe I'll see you on the mountain, yeah? Bring your biggest gun...
"The Third Man" was added.
(That meathead seemed bent on going up the mountain. I'd better tell Okudera-han.)
Well, if it isn't the guy whose face will be nowhere!
You sure ya should be usin' dynamite on someone else's mountain?
What's the problem? I'm going to get rid of their dangerous giant bear for them. They should be grateful.
They ain't never agreed to this. And for a young pup, ya sure are cocky 'bout Yama-oroshi.
Oh, and you being grizzled and grey makes you tough, huh? I'll have you know, I'm confident because I'm a master hunter. The brute doesn't stand a chance.
Why ya after Yama-oroshi, anyway?
Heh. For the money and fame, obviously! I mean, I guess there's the thrill of the hunt, too.
Thrill?
Heck yeah. Chasing your quarry down... outsmarting it, watching it drop. Knowing you've won nature's most primal contest. There's nothing like it.
Killin's a fun hobby for ya?
What's with the look? They're animals. It's not like I'm killing people.
Anyway, aren't you out here doing the same thing? Good luck trying to beat me.
(The man's trouble, but it ain't my place to stop 'im. Better just tell Okudera-han what's happenin' on the mountain.)
Okudera-san will be so happy to see you.
How's Okudera-han? Any better?
Sadly no.
I found him like this when I came to discuss Narumi. It's the wound from his fight with Yama-oroshi.
Pretty bad?
Yeah. He pushes himself too hard for his age. Always wants to be the tough old man.
So whadda we do? Can't ya call an ambulance?
You okay there?
Sorry. But no, that won't work. In this weather not even a helicopter could fly in, let alone an ambulance. We're just too remote.
So what <Italic>can</Italic> we do?
In the old days, drinking bear bile was the cure-all for this sort of thing. And it actually did work.
...An' now ya don't have any?
No.
Simple, then. I'll go get some.

I thought you might say that. But you have to realize,
this is a bear. It's not like hunting deer and rabbits.
"If ya kill, be ready to get killed." That's what Okudera-han always says.
I owe 'im. And I don't want Nishina to hafta go out huntin' right now.
So I'll go. It's the best thing. For everyone.
All right. I'm just sorry that all the dangerous work seems to fall on you.
Don't let it bother ya. It's my decision.
Well, just tell me when you're ready to go. I'll have Okudera-san's gun and supplies ready.
Will do. Thanks.
"Kill or Be Killed" was added.
You made it back!
Now there's a blessing. You can always replace objects, but you can't do the same for your life. Speaking of objects, I'll hold your gun and shells so you can sort out your things!
Let me know when you're going to the mountain again. And be better prepared this time!
You should remember you can always replace things, but not your life. Speaking of things, I'll hold onto your gun and shells.
Saejima-san, are you ready to go?
(Better say my farewells and leave for Tsukimino.)
I need a bit more time.
Okay. Okudera's condition is worrisome, but you're right⑬you need to be good and ready before you go.
Yeah. Ready to go.
Good, pack your snow gear.
Are you ready to go up now?
All right. It's time I explained the most important thing of all⑬hunting bears.
I'm all ears.
Hunters usually aim for a bear's heart, but that's pretty difficult for rookies.
That's why I think you should just aim for the head. If you manage to shoot it there, you'll still drop it with one shot.
One shot to the head. Okay.
That's right, and make it count! A wounded bear is a demon incarnate.
Got it. Message received.
Another thing: bears tend to roam around further up the mountain.
The best thing to do is just look for their tracks, and follow those.
Always be careful when you're tracking a bear. You don't want it to see you!
If it does see you and attacks, whatever you do, don't try to run.
You heard me. A bear runs faster than any man. It will catch you in no time, and then it's all over for you.
Instead of running, your best chance is to stay calm, stand your ground, and keep dodging its attacks until it wears itself out.
If a bear is watching you closely enough, it'll see where you point your gun, and dodge your shots. On the other hand, when it's charging, it's not in defense mode.
That's when you make your move. While the bear is charging, aim between its eyes. You'll drop it dead in its tracks with one shot. Easier said than done, of course.
Sure sounds like it.
But we're still counting on you! Here, take this. It can distract bears.
You got <Color:8>Bear Bait<Color:Default>.
Be careful out there. Don't do anything reckless.
All right. I'll hold onto your mountain gear.
No. We should be leavin' for Tsukimino.
Sorry I took so long.
Somehow. And I got the bear bile.
Incredible... All right, let me fix it up.
The fever's broken. I think he's through the worst of it.
That's good.
How was it, taking on a bear?
It was different from fightin' Yama-oroshi. With that monster, I jus' felt pure adrenaline. Like I didn't even think about what I was fightin'.
But this time, it wasn't like that. I had a gun, and I wasn't facin' Yama-oroshi. So I could think better. All that said, it was still terrifyin'.
Now I know what it feels like to face somethin' stronger than any man.
And to be honest... it makes me understand Okudera-han even less than I did before.
What's drivin' him to keep after an enemy like that?
...Who knows?
Say, I been meanin' to ask⑬why are ya on Okudera-han's side? Seems not many are.
Heh, if anything, I'm more alarmed by him than "on his side." I worry about his total disregard for safety.
Then again... maybe I envy him.
Yer envious?
To understand why, you have to remember... This village is a tiny world unto itself. To survive here, you have to get along with others, no matter the cost.
That means swallowing one's pride and stifling one's conscience, for the sake of fitting in.
But Okudera doesn't do that. He doesn't care what the others think. He doesn't even care about his own life...
He's true to himself, and he's got the determination of an ox. So, I admire him for having principles.
Principles, huh?
...Yes. I have to go now. Uh, Narumi, was it? We'll have to keep an eye on him.
Unfortunately, bear bile's not an easy thing to get.
I can help you, though. I'll hold onto the gun and ammo for now, and you can go sort your things.
Let me know when you're leaving for the mountain. You've got a lot to prepare!
This could be a long outing. Are you sure you're ready?
(Better bid farewell to Okudera-han, then head to Tsukimino...)
All right. Be quick, though!
Yup. Ready.
Good. Pack up your snow gear.
Are you ready to go up?
Looks like you're ready to go⑬great! Now, we think Narumi scattered his bait in an area stretching from the foot of the mountain to midway up the peak.
I marked the likely locations of the bait on your map, so that should make it easier for you.
But it'll also be dangerous, because I'm sure plenty of bears have been drawn to the bait by now. Be careful.
Oh, all right. I'll hold on to your snow gear for you.
No. We gotta leave for Tsukimino.
So, Narumi's hurt.
Yeah. He's in trouble. Needs help.
Hmph. Can't say I'm very motivated to help him. On the other hand, it sure would be a nuisance if he died on the mountain.
Fine. I'll tell Nishina. You get some rest. And by the way... thanks for all your efforts.
Okudera-han, a lot's happenin' out there while you been sleepin'...
Makes you quieter while walking in a crouch.
I guess your search for bear bait isn't going so well.
Well, don't let it bother you too much. I'll hold onto your gun and ammunition while you get your equipment sorted.
Let me know when you're leaving for the mountain. You've got a lot to prepare for!
Saejima-san, are you ready?
Need a bit more time.
All right. I'm just sorry that all the tough work seems to fall on you.
Yup, ready.
Good. Get your equipment ready.
Sorry you have to do this. But if Narumi's injured, there's no time to waste.
Leave it to me.
We gave you first aid, but you need to go to the hospital in Tsukimino as soon as possible.
The road there is actually open now. You're lucky beyond words.
Sakurai, can you call him a taxi?
Yes, I can.
I'm... so sorry...
If you truly are, then never come back here. That's all the apology we need.
Hehehe. I wouldn't come back if you begged me.
Nishina-san, the taxi will be here soon.
Give this to that old guy for me, will you?
Narumi handed over the Vertical Double Special.
It shoots transmitters. Shoot your quarry with one, and you can track its position.
I thought I could track that monster, but I won't have the chance now.
It probably won't work if you shoot it into the beast's back or legs. Heck, when I tried, it looked like my shots were bouncing right off it.
But I think it'll work if you shoot it into its soft underbelly.
Nice idea. I'll try it.
We should get going.
This injury... I'll never be able to carry a gun again. What am I supposed to live for now?
You'll have to find somethin'. You're lucky ya still have that opportunity. Maybe ya oughta keep that in mind.
The search for Narumi's not going well, huh?
If it makes it any easier, I can hold your gun and shells while you get your stuff sorted.
Do you have any idea what you've done? Did you even think about what this could do to us!?
Hah. Of course I did.
I was thinking about what a favor I was doing for you all. Or did you <Italic>want</Italic> to keep living terrified of some bear?
It's not some bear! It's Yama-oroshi.
See, that's what I'm talking about! You people have made this animal into some kind of god figure.
Everyone! Pipe down a sec. What happened, exactly?
These country bumpkins... They don't want anyone to take real action to solve a problem, I guess.
This braying jackass has been scattering bear bait all over the mountain!
What? Why're you doin' that?
He's trying to lure out Yama-oroshi. We'll all be in danger!
Why? Ya think he'll come down here to the village?
Not only that, all the other bears are going to smell the food, too. They'll wake up from hibernation.
...And they'll be crazed as a pack of wild dogs on the hunt!
They're sure to bring their feeding frenzy to our village!

So what? I'll kill the whole damn lot. All the bears I can shoot!
This'll be the hunting trip of a lifetime.
Hey! Nishina-san!
There was another bear sighting!
Was it Yama-oroshi?
They couldn't tell; it took off right away. But they said it was huge.
Okay. Someone needs to tell everyone to get inside.
I'll do it.
That's right, you people go home and cower in a corner. That'll keep you out of my way!
Jerk.
Is there anything else we can do?
It's not too late to stop this. We can go pick up all the bait.
But some bears are out and hungry already. We need all the men to stand guard.
I'll go get the bait. You two stay with the others to protect the village.
Nishina-san?
We accept your help.
I know eight spots on the mountain where an experienced hunter would put bait. I'll mark them on a map for you. Got it?
I'll get a pack ready for you at Okudera-san's. Meet me there.
This is going to require a lot more time on the mountain compared to your last trip, so prep thoroughly, all right?
We're counting on you!
"Hubris" was added.
I think that should be enough food for your expedition. But please, be careful out there.
Are you the man who saw Yama-oroshi?
Yup. May I ask yer name too, ma'am?
Kimiyo Nishina. Nishina is my husband.
Oh yeah, I met 'im. The hunter fella who's the village chief.
(If she's married to him, she prob'ly thinks bad of Okudera, too.)
I hope you don't intend to go into the woods.
Well, that ain't why I came callin', at least.
Oh. Did you come looking for food, perhaps?
...How'd ya know that?
I remember that day nine years ago... when Okudera-san came to ask for food, just like you're doing now.
You may have heard... Nine years ago, Okudera-san went to the mountain in search of his hunter friend.
He was determined to help, even though there was a horrible blizzard that day. And he knew that going out there without any food was suicide.
So Okudera-han came 'round here lookin' for food?
He came 'round everywhere. He went from one house to the other, head bowed, hat in hand. But... well, no one wanted to share their food with an outsider.
